title: Weibull-MBUR {Y} A New Family of Generalized Unit Distributions with Correlated Parameters: Is the Correlation, Distribution or Data Driven or Interaction Between Them
content: Generalizing a distribution can be achieved by inserting one or more new parameters to the baseline distribution. The author deliberates this methodology to build, Weibull Median Based Unit Rayleigh {Y} family of distributions. The author applies the approach of the T-X{Y} family to add more than one parameter to the baseline distribution Median Based Unit Rayleigh (MBUR) defined on the unit interval with one parameter b > 0. The generator distribution is the Weibull distribution with the two parameters, c & ξ > 0, the shape and scale parameters respectively as will be explained in the paper. The author consumed different link distributions or Y distributions in the form of the quantile function of this link distribution to link the baseline distribution, the MBUR, to the generator distribution, the Weibull distribution. The link distributions deployed are the Lomax, Dagum, exponential, exponentiated exponential and the Log Logistic distributions. This technique results in new different distributions with different number of parameters, as will be discussed in the paper. For each new distribution, the author derived the PDF, CDF, quantile and hazard functions as well as the raw moments. The author expands some of the PDFs in a linear series expansion that is simple and does not require special function. This makes the computational statistics for the raw moments easier and simpler. The supplementary material associated with the paper contains figures for the PDF, CDF and the Hazard functions. Real data analysis reveals correlation between the parameters of the new distributions. The author clarified this by comparing the fitness of the new distributions to the same dataset, rate of recovery from COVID 19 in Spain, to wonder whether this correlation is data dependent or distribution dependent or mix and interaction between both the data and the distribution.
